rationale: Workers do destroy surplus queen cells and may kill or expel rival queens, but the claim overstates how routinely they kill most queens and assigns a specific colony-level purpose.
Honey bees show strong floral constancy during individual foraging bouts, although switches between plant species can occur within a trip.
Documented human births have produced more than five infants, including surviving higher-order multiples.
Honey-bee age polyethism generally runs in the opposite direction: younger workers perform in-hive tasks and older workers forage outside.
Sharks and rays lack the bony operculum typical of most bony fishes, but attributing that absence simply to a cartilaginous skeleton is an unsupported causal explanation.
Most naturally horned mammals are even-toed ungulates, while living equids are single-hoofed and do not bear paired horns.
Dolphins are viviparous and have paired mammary glands concealed in slits on the ventral surface near the genital opening.
In the usual insect mating arrangement, the male transfers sperm through an intromittent organ into the female, not the reverse as universally asserted here.
Monotremes have hair but lay eggs, providing clear exceptions to the universal claim.
Elephant gestation is exceptionally long, roughly 18 to 22 months, and births are usually singletons, but twins occur and a strict two-year duration is imprecise.
Male catfish in this group provide prolonged nest and fry defense, and the reported duration is biologically plausible, though it is unlikely to be fixed at forty to fifty days.
European eels reproduce sexually from eggs; they do not arise spontaneously from worms in mud.
The conspicuous sound-producing organs and calling behavior of cicadas are male traits used principally in mate attraction.
Rabies infects and can kill humans as well as other mammals, while exposure does not guarantee infection in every bitten animal.
Hair does not continue biological growth after death; skin dehydration and retraction can merely make hairs appear longer.
Normal adult tooth counts are not systematically greater in males than females in humans or the named livestock.
Many interspecific hybrids besides mules are sterile or have strongly reduced fertility, especially in one sex.
Sperm are produced by specialized germ-line tissues and carry genetic information; semen is not a physical contribution drawn from every body part.
Partridges and many other ground-nesting birds perform distraction displays that simulate injury to draw predators away from chicks.
Egg and larval mortality is generally high in broadcast-spawning fishes, and high fecundity is an evolved life-history response associated with that mortality.

Octopuses have eight long arms, while squid and cuttlefish have eight shorter arms plus two tentacles; the statement captures the arm comparison but is incomplete if all appendages are counted as feet.
Brown bears commonly give birth in winter dens, fast during denning, and emerge with cubs in spring, though timing and complete fasting vary.
Some bony fishes are live-bearing, and cartilaginous fishes include many egg-laying species as well as several forms of viviparity.
European eels reproduce sexually and possess gonads and reproductive ducts, even though these mature late during oceanic migration.
Several sharks are placentally viviparous, with embryos initially using yolk and later receiving maternal support through a uterine connection.
Visible age-related greying occurs in numerous mammals, including dogs and other primates, not only humans and horses.
Argonauts use expanded arm membranes in shell formation and swimming, but the romanticized use of a membrane as a wind sail is not supported.
Spider-hunting and mud-nesting wasps do provision sealed nests with spiders, but prey are often paralyzed rather than killed and eggs, not already formed grubs, are laid with them.
The typical human skeleton has twelve pairs of ribs, not eight.
Partridges require transfer of sperm for fertilization; wind, calls, breath, or an overhead flight cannot impregnate a female.
The right kidney is higher in some taxa but lower in humans because of the liver, so the universal anatomical claim is false.
A honey-bee queen lays the fertilized eggs that develop into both workers and new queens, with caste determined chiefly by rearing conditions.
Swans vocalize in ordinary social and reproductive contexts; there is no sound evidence that they chiefly sing as death approaches.
Elephants are capable swimmers and can hold the trunk above water as a snorkel while the rest of the body is submerged.
Humans have large brains relative to body size but are not uniquely maximal by all scaling measures, and 'moistest' is neither a supported nor useful comparative distinction.
In temperate annual social-wasp colonies, workers usually die before or during winter while newly produced queens overwinter in sheltered sites, with some variation among species and climates.
Female octopuses guard and aerate their eggs, generally cease feeding, lose substantial condition, and die after brooding.
A worker honey bee commonly dies after its barbed sting lodges in elastic mammalian skin and tears out associated abdominal tissues, though it can withdraw the sting from some targets.
Crocodiles move the lower jaw at its joint like other vertebrates; raising the head and upper jaw can create a misleading visual impression.
Crabs, crayfish, and lobsters repeatedly molt their exoskeletons as they grow and are soft immediately after a molt.
European eels are catadromous and leave fresh or brackish waters for the sea, while grey mullets commonly move from coastal waters into estuaries, lagoons, and rivers.
Routine killing of the mother by newly hatched offspring is not a general feature of scorpion or spider reproduction, although rare maternal consumption occurs in some spiders.
Many temperate reptiles reduce feeding and activity in winter, but the four-month duration, total fasting, and inclusion of all named taxa across their ranges are overgeneralizations.
Molluscs, tunicates, and barnacles develop through sexual or asexual reproduction from pre-existing organisms, not spontaneous generation from substrate.
Donkeys can be infested by both lice and ticks, and ectoparasitism is not literally universal among every other bird and mammal.
Brains contain an extensive blood-vessel network and circulating blood and are metabolically warm in living endotherms.
Many raptors aggregate or flock, particularly vultures, migrating hawks, and some social hunting species.
The listed birds generally migrate, disperse, or remain active rather than spending winter hidden; occasional torpor in swallows does not support the broad claim.

Some Mediterranean serranids are simultaneous hermaphrodites, so all adults can possess ovaries, but the absolute assertion that specimens are always caught full of eggs is too strong and the identifications are uncertain.
Cuckoos and hawks are unquestionably distinct species with different anatomy, although the supporting assertion that members of one species never prey on one another is false.
Newborn human eye color varies and is not universally blue, while postnatal eye-color change is also visible in other animals.
The named horned ruminants lack upper incisors, have a four-compartment stomach, and regurgitate and rechew cud.
Segregation and recombination can make inherited traits and family resemblance absent or subtle in one generation and conspicuous in a later one.
The brain is central to sensory processing, whereas the heart is not the sensory center; the brain tissue's own limited pain sensation does not imply sensory irrelevance.
The male octopus hectocotylus is a specialized reproductive arm that transfers spermatophores into the female mantle cavity.
Several well-documented animals, including bowhead whales and some turtles and fishes, can live longer than humans.
Pigeons and doves commonly form durable socially monogamous pair bonds, but divorce and extra-pair mating occur and bonds are not invariably lifelong.
Tusks and horns occupy largely different mammalian groups, but species such as muntjacs combine antlers with enlarged canine teeth, defeating a strict universal formulation.
Common kingfishers normally breed in spring and summer rather than around the winter solstice.
Sessile animals commonly reproduce sexually and may be separate-sexed or hermaphroditic; immobility does not imply absence of sex.
Electric rays generate strong electrical discharges with specialized organs to stun prey and can deliver perceptible shocks to humans.
Fishes suffer transmissible epidemic diseases caused by viruses, bacteria, fungi, and parasites, sometimes with mass mortality.
Fig wasps develop in caprifigs and enter receptive cultivated figs, enabling pollination and fruit retention in varieties that require caprification.
Removing a young cock's testes suppresses crowing, comb development, and sexual behavior, but cauterizing the rump is not itself a reliable description of castration.
The famous crocodile-tooth-cleaning bird story lacks reliable evidence of a regular mutualistic behavior in wild Nile crocodiles.
Common cuckoos are obligate brood parasites that lay one egg per host nest and leave rearing to the host, but the female more often removes a host egg than devours the whole clutch.
Male sharks, skates, and rays have a pair of pelvic claspers used in mating, while females lack them.
Water commonly retains heat and is warmer than night air, and crocodiles often remain in water at night, though their habitat use has multiple causes and varies with conditions.
Honey bees collect floral nectar and enzymatically transform and dehydrate it into honey; it is not atmospheric dew gathered ready-made.

Prepubertal castration prevents normal androgen-driven voice deepening and much terminal hair growth and greatly reduces androgenic baldness, but 'never goes bald' is too absolute because other causes remain.
Embryonic organs and structures differentiate in an ordered sequence rather than all existing in mature form from the beginning.
Many mobile animals, including earthworms, snails, and numerous fishes, are simultaneous or sequential hermaphrodites rather than separate-sexed individuals.
Smooth-hound sharks include placentally viviparous forms in which the yolk sac forms a maternal connection after yolk is depleted, with fetal membranes surrounding the embryo.
Fishes hear through inner ears and lateral-line-associated mechanics and smell through well-developed olfactory organs and nasal openings.
Heritable variants can cause similar congenital conditions in parent and child, but acquired lameness, blindness, scars, and pimples are not inherited as matching marks.
Female-biased size dimorphism is widespread across insects because fecundity often favors larger females, although male-biased size occurs in important groups.
Egg shape does not determine or reliably reveal a chick's sex, which is set genetically at fertilization in domestic fowl.
Claw asymmetry and handedness vary among decapod species and individuals; the right claw is not invariably larger in crabs or crayfish.
Canine gestation averages about 63 days, but viable births can occur outside the asserted strict sixty-to-sixty-three-day range depending on how gestation is measured.
Hyenas have distinct sexes rather than each possessing both sets of genitalia, while especially in spotted hyenas the female external genitalia can resemble those of males.
Normal human semen is whitish regardless of ancestry, and mammalian semen is generally pale, though 'invariably' fails under normal variation, disease, and the diversity of animals.
Presentation varies among viviparous animals, with breech births possible and tail-first delivery normal in cetaceans and some other taxa.
All living cetaceans are mammals and give birth to live young after internal gestation rather than laying eggs.
Octopuses rapidly alter chromatophore and skin patterns for camouflage during hunting and in response to threat.
Lions have the standard mammalian series of seven cervical vertebrae, not one continuous neck bone.
Many short-lived birds, particularly small passerines, routinely breed in the first breeding season after hatching.
Eagle pairs often defend large territories and juveniles disperse after independence, but they do not categorically exclude all other birds from settling nearby.
The embryonic chick heart is among the earliest functioning organs, appears as a pulsating blood-containing structure, and connects to developing vessels.

Common cranes migrate from Eurasian breeding grounds to northeastern Africa, including the Nile region, but the characterization of their destination as the Nile's source marshes is geographically imprecise.
Honey bees compensate for wind through flight control and behavior, but there is no credible evidence that they carry stones as ballast.
Females are larger than males in many sharks, rays, and fishes, often because fecundity favors body size, but this pattern is not universal across selachians or fishes.
Sperm production commonly begins around puberty near age fourteen, but males can be reproductively capable well before twenty-one.
Hens and geese ovulate and lay unfertilized eggs without any previous mating.
Acquired mutilations are generally not encoded in germ-line DNA, so offspring do not ordinarily reproduce a parent's injury.
The named carnivores produce altricial young with sealed eyelids that open after birth, although the broad anatomical category is not a precise causal rule.
Larvae of holometabolous insects feed and excrete, whereas the pupal stage in butterflies, bees, and wasps is generally nonfeeding and does not defecate.
Human cranial sutures follow the same basic anatomical pattern in both sexes, with individual variation rather than the asserted sex-specific counts.
Across animals there is a strong life-history tendency for larger species to produce fewer offspring per reproductive event than small species, despite many exceptions.
Anglerfish in this group conceal themselves and use a modified fin ray bearing a lure near the head to attract prey within striking distance.
Many sharks and bony fishes are internally viviparous while obtaining oxygen through gills rather than breathing air.

The vertebrate heart and vascular system form very early and the heart is often described as the first functional organ, but 'first distinctly formed in all vertebrates' is stronger than comparative embryology supports.
Other mammals show ticklish responses and laughter-like play vocalizations, so neither behavior is uniquely human.
